promptHead: Athlete goal: marathon (Wexley Lakes Marathon) on Sun Nov 1 2026, 10 weeks out, target under 3:45.

new.headline: New knee pain changes the plan: skip Wednesday's tempo, swap in cross-training, keep runs short and flat, and get the knee looked at before the next long run.

flags.title: Long run cut short

flags.title: New right-knee pain

answers.question: Is this an IT band thing? Should I still do Wednesday's tempo?
answers.answer:
I can't tell you what it is, and I shouldn't try. The pattern you describe (outside of the knee, worse on downhills, aches on stairs, new) is worth a visit to a sports physio or your doctor this week so you get a real answer and a plan. In the meantime we train around it.

No, skip Wednesday's tempo. One hard session on a knee that just stopped you mid-long-run can turn a one-week problem into a one-month problem. We replace it with cross-training and keep running easy and flat until the knee is quiet.

new.analysis:
## Why this plan

The knee is the only story this week. You were cruising through the build, long run building nicely from 10 to 11 to 12 mi, easy pace and heart rate ticking in the right direction, and then a new lateral knee pain shut Sunday down at 8.5 mi. That is a correction worth taking seriously, not pushing through.

So the week pulls back on purpose. Volume drops, the tempo comes out, and Wednesday becomes cross-training so you keep aerobic work without pounding the knee. Everything that stays on foot is short, flat and conversational, which protects the knee and still keeps the legs turning over.

The long run is capped at 8 mi on a flat route, and only if the knee is quiet by Sunday. We would rather do 8 pain-free miles than chase 13 and lose two weeks. With 10 weeks to the race there is still plenty of runway: one careful week now costs us nothing, a flare-up costs us a month.

Please get the knee looked at this week. If a professional clears you and the pain is gone, we rebuild the long run and bring the tempo back next week. If it is still sore, we hold the pattern and reassess.

safetyCallouts.title: See a sports physio or your doctor about the knee this week.
safetyCallouts.body: New, sharp pain on the outside of the knee that stopped you mid-run and still aches on stairs is worth a proper look before the next long run. I can't diagnose it. If pain gets worse, swells, or you can't walk normally, stop running and get seen sooner. Keep training easy and flat until a professional clears you.
